text: [BLOCKER] AlphaFold3 is never invoked; every "AF3" pLDDT, PAE, and 3D coordinate is a hardcoded trigonometric/ASCII expression — The platform's central claim is that it "models 25 De Novo Targeted Bio-Conjugate Therapeutics designed via AlphaFold3" and provides "direct live integration with the official AlphaFold Server" (README.md:22-24). No AlphaFold3 model, API, or output file is present or contacted anywhere. `grep -nE "fetch\(|XMLHttpRequest|WebSocket|axios|\.ajax|EventSource" app.js` returns zero matches -- app.js performs no network I/O whatsoever. The three artifacts presented as AlphaFold3 output are closed-form functions of the string index and the ASCII code point of the residue letter: (a) app.js:791 `let score = 93 + Math.sin(i * 0.4) * 4 + (char.charCodeAt(0) % 5) * 0.5;` labelled at app.js:803 as `'AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score'`; (b) app.js:850 `let error = Math.abs(i - j) * 0.4 + (sequence.charCodeAt(i % sequence.length) % 4) * 0.3;` rendered under the index.html:397 heading "2D PAE (Predicted Aligned Error) Domain Matrix (0 - 30 Å)"; (c) app.js:715-726, a cylindrical helix with `radius = 6 + (charCode % 5) * 0.8`, `pitch = (i - seqLength/2) * 0.6`, `angle = (i/seqLength) * Math.PI * (charCode % 3 === 0 ? 6 : 4)`, introduced by the app.js:707 comment `// REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING & 3D BACKBONE TOPOLOGY GENERATION` and titled at index.html:377 "Real Sequence 3D Structure (pLDDT Color Spectrum)". The helix has no relationship to protein geometry: backbone phi/psi torsions, Ramachandran-allowed regions, 3.8 Å Ca-Ca spacing, secondary structure, and steric exclusion are all absent. index.html:42 renders a status pill reading "AlphaFold Server Live Connected" whose entire implementation is `<a href="https://alphafoldserver.com/" target="_blank">` -- a hyperlink, not a connection. Consequence: This is not a gap in an otherwise working tool; it is the absence of the tool. A reviewer, collaborator, or funder opening the "25 De Novo Drug Center" sees a per-residue confidence curve, a PAE heatmap, and a rotating 3D model rendered under AlphaFold3 headings, and has no way from the interface to know that the underlying computation is `Math.sin`. The pLDDT curve is the single most load-bearing number in modern structural biology -- it is what practitioners use to decide whether a predicted region is trustworthy enough to design against. Presenting a sine wave under that label transfers false confidence directly into downstream decisions: which of the 25 candidates to synthesize, which loop to mutate, which region to trust. Because the platform is self-described as a drug discovery platform, the harm is not abstract -- it is a wet-lab budget spent on a candidate ranked by a trigonometric function.

text: Required fix for SWE-01: Either implement the claimed capability or remove the claim. To implement: run AlphaFold3 (via the AlphaFold Server for eligible non-commercial use, or via the google-deepmind/alphafold3 code with obtained weights, or a permissively licensed reimplementation such as Boltz or Chai-1) for each of the 35 sequences; commit the resulting mmCIF and confidence JSON to a versioned `data/structures/<candidate_id>/` directory with a checksum manifest; replace `initModal3DCanvas`, `renderModalPlddtChart`, and `renderModalPaeHeatmap` with loaders that parse those files and render via Mol*; delete every synthetic generator. To remove the claim: strip "AlphaFold3" and "AlphaFold Server Live Connected" from index.html:6, :30, :42, :54, :265, :290, :371, :377, :383, :397 and from README.md:1, :22, :24, :106-111; relabel each generated series in the UI as "Illustrative placeholder -- not a structure prediction"; and add a persistent banner on the modal stating that no structure prediction has been performed.

text: Ground truth for SWE-01: AlphaFold3 (Abramson et al., Nature 630, 2024, DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w) produces, per prediction, an mmCIF coordinate file plus a JSON confidence bundle containing per-atom/per-residue pLDDT, the full N×N PAE matrix, pTM and ipTM. pLDDT is a learned per-residue estimate of the expected lDDT-Ca of the prediction against the true structure; it is emitted by the confidence head of a trained network and is not analytically expressible. PAE_ij is the expected positional error in residue j when the prediction and truth are aligned on residue i -- a genuinely pairwise quantity, whereas app.js:850 makes the second term depend only on the row index i, so it is a per-row constant offset carrying no pairwise information. A platform that claims AF3 provenance must ship the actual AF3 output files (mmCIF + confidence JSON), parse pLDDT from the B-factor column or the confidence JSON, and render the real PAE matrix; the established open-source component for exactly this is Mol* (Sehnal et al., Nucleic Acids Research, 2021, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkab314), which the RCSB PDB, PDBe, and the AlphaFold DB all use in production.

text: [BLOCKER] Identical sequences are published as distinct candidates carrying mutually contradictory pLDDT and ΔG values — Programmatic extraction of all 25 `sequence` fields and all 10 `fasta` fields shows that 7 distinct sequences account for 16 records, and every reused sequence carries different numbers in each copy. `KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG` (36 aa) appears three times: app.js:153 drug 2 HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 at ΔG -16.2, Kd 2.1 nM, pLDDT 94.8; app.js:247 drug 11 BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1 at ΔG -17.5, Kd 0.65 nM, pLDDT 94.3; app.js:131 candidate rank 7 CogAChE-PAS-02 at ΔG -12.6, pLDDT 92.8. `SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC` (41 aa) appears three times at ΔG -16.5 / -15.7 / -12.1 and pLDDT 93.2 / 92.8 / 90.7, and is simultaneously assigned to the α7 nAChR ECD (drug 6) and to the TLR4/MD-2 complex (drug 18) -- two unrelated receptors. `VRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH` appears at app.js:205 (TrkB, ΔG -17.2, pLDDT 95.8) and app.js:361 (EAAT2/GLT-1, ΔG -15.8, pLDDT 94.1). `CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH` appears at app.js:173 (Frizzled-8, ΔG -16.9, pLDDT 95.1) and app.js:371 (ZO-1/occludin, ΔG -16.1, pLDDT 93.8). Three further pairs behave the same way. pLDDT differs by up to 4.4 points and ΔG by up to 4.4 kcal/mol for byte-identical input. Separately, every one of the 25 ΔG/Kd pairs violates ΔG = RT·ln(Kd): at 298.15 K, ΔG = -18.4 kcal/mol implies Kd = 3.3e-5 nM, not the stated 0.32 nM; the stated Kd 0.32 nM implies ΔG = -12.95 kcal/mol. The discrepancy across all 25 records ranges from 3.45 to 5.73 kcal/mol -- four to five orders of magnitude in Kd -- and is not even a constant offset, so it is not a unit-convention artifact. Consequence: pLDDT is a deterministic function of the model, the input sequence, and the random seed. Even granting AF3's diffusion-sampling stochasticity, seed-to-seed pLDDT variation on a confident peptide is well under a point, and a 4.4-point spread on identical input cannot be produced by seed noise. More decisively, ΔG against two different receptors cannot be a property of the ligand alone -- yet here the same molecule is assigned different ΔG values against the same receptor (drugs 2 and 11 both target AChE). Combined with the thermodynamic inconsistency of all 25 ΔG/Kd pairs, the only reading consistent with the evidence is that these numbers were written by hand rather than computed. Any expert who does what I just did -- sort the sequences -- reaches that conclusion in under five minutes, and at that point every remaining number in the repository becomes unusable, including any that might happen to be right. This also means the "25 therapeutics" and "TOP 10 candidates" counts are inflated: at the level of distinct molecular entities the pipeline contains 28 unique sequences across 35 records, and the leaderboard rankings are not comparisons between different designs.

text: Required fix for SWE-02: Add a uniqueness constraint on the canonicalized sequence across the entire dataset and resolve the 7 collisions -- either by merging the duplicate records into single entities, or by supplying the genuinely distinct sequences that were intended. Add a CI assertion `abs(dg - R*T*log(kd_molar)) < tol` with T and tol declared explicitly, and either recompute every ΔG from its Kd or every Kd from its ΔG so the pair is self-consistent. Attach to every ΔG a `method` field naming the actual calculation (MM/GBSA, FEP, empirical scoring function, or "design target -- not computed") and a `uncertainty` field; a ΔG with no method and no error bar should fail validation. Until these numbers are recomputed by a named method, mark every affinity and pLDDT value in the UI as a hypothetical design target rather than a computed result.

text: Ground truth for SWE-02: ΔG° = -RT·ln(Ka) = RT·ln(Kd). With R = 1.9872e-3 kcal·mol⁻¹·K⁻¹ and T = 298.15 K, RT = 0.5925 kcal/mol, so ΔG(kcal/mol) = 0.5925 · ln(Kd/1 M); a 1 nM binder corresponds to ΔG = -12.27 kcal/mol and -18.4 kcal/mol corresponds to Kd = 33 fM. This identity is not optional -- it is the definition of the dissociation constant -- and a two-line assertion catches every one of these 25 records. On duplicate detection: a primary-key/uniqueness constraint on the canonicalized sequence is the standard mechanism (it is what ChEMBL, UniProt, and the PDB all enforce), and RDKit's InChIKey plays the same role for small molecules. Best practice for the affinity numbers themselves is set out in "Best Practices for Alchemical Free Energy Calculations" (Living Journal of Computational Molecular Science, 2020, DOI 10.33011/livecoms.2.1.18378), which requires that every reported binding free energy carry a method, a force field, a sampling protocol, and an uncertainty estimate.

text: [CRITICAL] No schema, type, unit, or range validation exists anywhere; scientific values are packed inside human-readable prose strings — There is no schema file, no type annotation, no validator, and no assertion in the repository (verified: `schemas/` absent, no `assert` in app.js). Every scientific quantity is embedded inside an English sentence. app.js:146 stores affinity as the single string `"ΔG = -18.4 kcal/mol | Kd = 0.32 nM | AF3 pLDDT = 96.2 / 100"` and app.js:147 stores safety as `"hERG IC50 > 50 μM (0% Cardiotoxicity) | Seizure Index: 0.01 | Downregulation: < 3.5%"`. Three numbers with three different units, plus a categorical claim, plus an inequality operator, in one untyped string. The only consumer is positional splitting at app.js:562-563 (`drug.affinity.split('|')[0].trim()` / `[1].trim()`), which throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')` on any record with fewer than two pipes -- a one-character edit away from a blank page. Four concrete corruptions already sit in the data and would be caught by any schema: (1) app.js:381 the `sequence` field of drug 24 AstroPafr-Block-A4 is `"His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate"`, English prose, not a sequence -- yet it is passed to `initModal3DCanvas`, `renderModalPlddtChart` (producing residue labels `H1`, `i2`, `s3`, `-4`, `1`5), `renderModalPaeHeatmap`, and to the "Copy FASTA Sequence" button at index.html:362, which would paste it into the AlphaFold Server input box; (2) the non-standard residue letter `B` (the Asx ambiguity code, not a proteinogenic amino acid and not accepted as protein input by AlphaFold Server) appears in app.js:173, :371, and :130; (3) app.js:60 and :70 store `"C58H92O27 (Onjisaponin V Core Skeleton)"` and `"C36H30O16 (Caffeic Acid Tetramer)"` in fields named `smiles` -- molecular formulas, which are not SMILES; (4) app.js:50, the curcumin `smiles` value, ends `...C=C2)O)OCH3)O`, and bare `CH3` is not valid SMILES (H is only legal inside brackets), so this string fails to parse in RDKit or OpenBabel. Consequence: The direct question posed by the review -- could a typo in a ΔG ever be caught? -- has a definitive answer: no. Nothing reads these values as numbers, so `-18.4` becoming `-184` or `18.4` would render, pass unnoticed, and propagate into the drug cards and the leaderboard. The four corruptions above are the proof: they are already present, already shipped, and already rendered without complaint. The string-packing also makes the entire dataset programmatically unusable -- you cannot sort candidates by Kd, filter by pLDDT threshold, plot ΔG against molecular weight, join against ChEMBL, or run a unit check, because there are no numbers, only sentences. That is what "unusable programmatically" means concretely, and it is why the ΔG/Kd inconsistency in SWE-02 survived into a published artifact: no code path ever compared them. Worst of all is the drug-24 case, where a UI button offers to copy a non-sequence to the user's clipboard for submission to a real external structure-prediction service.

text: Required fix for SWE-03: Move all data out of app.js into `data/*.json` and write `schemas/*.schema.json` declaring every field. Replace each prose string with typed fields: `delta_g_kcal_per_mol` (number, maximum 0), `kd_nM` (number, exclusiveMinimum 0), `plddt` (number, 0-100), `herg_ic50_uM` (number plus a separate `operator` enum for `>`), `seizure_index` (number, 0-1). Constrain `sequence` with `"pattern": "^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]+$"` -- this rejects drug 24 and the three B-containing records immediately. Add a CI step that runs the JSON Schema validator, an RDKit round-trip over every SMILES field, and the ΔG/Kd consistency assertion from SWE-02, and fails the build on any error. Delete the positional `split('|')` parsing at app.js:562-563 in favour of reading the typed fields directly.

text: Ground truth for SWE-03: Scientific data layers separate value, unit, and provenance into distinct typed fields -- `{"delta_g": {"value": -18.4, "unit": "kcal/mol", "method": "...", "uncertainty": 0.8}}` -- and validate them mechanically. The two standard mechanisms are JSON Schema (declarative, language-neutral, runs in CI) and Pydantic v2 (runtime, Python, with custom validators). The pattern is a core element of the FAIR Guiding Principles (Wilkinson et al., Scientific Data 3:160018, 2016, DOI 10.1038/sdata.2016.18), specifically I1 ("formal, accessible, shared and broadly applicable language for knowledge representation") and R1 ("richly described with a plurality of accurate and relevant attributes"), and of "Best Practices for Scientific Computing" (PLoS Biology, 2014, DOI 10.1371/journal.pbio.1001745), which states the rule as: make the data machine-readable and check it automatically. Protein sequence validity is `^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]+$` for standard residues -- B, J, O, U, X, Z are ambiguity or non-standard codes that AlphaFold Server rejects. SMILES validity is checked by round-tripping through `rdkit.Chem.MolFromSmiles`, which returns None on failure.

text: [CRITICAL] Not reproducible or installable by anyone: no manifest, no environment, no tests, no CI, no version, and a run instruction that is an absolute path on the author's laptop — The complete documented installation and execution procedure is README.md:119-124: "Clone this repository or open the project folder. Open `index.html` directly in any web browser: `file:///Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/index.html`". The sole run instruction is an absolute filesystem path inside one named user's home directory -- it is not portable to any other machine, and it discloses the author's OS username. There is no dependency manifest of any kind, so the three runtime dependencies (Three.js, OrbitControls, Chart.js) are undeclared and undiscoverable except by reading the HTML. There is no test suite and no test framework: `grep -rnE "describe\(|it\(|test\(|expect\(|assert" app.js` returns only two false positives from `split('|')`. There is no CI configuration -- `.github/` does not exist. There is no version identifier anywhere: no `version` field (no manifest to hold one), no git tag, no `__version__`, no CHANGELOG. There is no LICENSE file, no CITATION.cff, no CONTRIBUTING.md, and no code of conduct. Because `file://` origins block `fetch()` in Chrome and Safari, the stated launch method also forecloses the only architecturally correct fix for the data-layering problem -- loading data from external JSON -- so the current run instruction actively entrenches the inline-literal design. Consequence: Reproducibility is the property that a third party can obtain the same artifact and the same outputs from the same inputs. None of the necessary preconditions is present here. A reader cannot determine which Chart.js version produced the figures (see SWE-05), cannot pin an environment, cannot verify that the code still runs correctly after any change (no tests), cannot detect regressions (no CI), and cannot cite a specific state of the work (no version, no DOI). For JOSS specifically these are hard requirements, not preferences: the review checklist requires an OSI-approved license in the repository, installation instructions, example usage, functionality documentation, automated tests or a documented manual test procedure, and community guidelines. This submission satisfies zero of the six and would be desk-rejected before a reviewer was assigned. Independent of JOSS, the absence of tests around a codebase whose entire purpose is to display numeric scientific values means there is no mechanism -- none -- by which a wrong number becomes a failing build.

text: Ground truth for SWE-04: "Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research" (PLoS Computational Biology, 2013, DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285) states the applicable rules directly: record how every result was produced, avoid manual data manipulation, archive the exact versions of all external programs used, and version-control all custom scripts. The FAIR principles (DOI 10.1038/sdata.2016.18) add F1 (globally unique and persistent identifiers -- i.e. versioned releases with DOIs) and R1.1 (a clear and accessible data usage license). "Best Practices for Scientific Computing" (DOI 10.1371/journal.pbio.1001745) adds: plan for mistakes by adding assertions and unit tests, and use a build tool to automate workflows. The modern packaging of this is RO-Crate ("Packaging research artefacts with RO-Crate", Data Science, 2022, DOI 10.3233/DS-210053), which bundles data, code, and machine-readable provenance into one citable archive.

text: Ground truth for SWE-05: The correct Three.js teardown, per the library's own "How to dispose of objects" guide, is: cancel the animation frame using the handle returned by `requestAnimationFrame`; traverse the scene calling `geometry.dispose()` and `material.dispose()` (and `texture.dispose()`) on every disposable; call `renderer.dispose()`; and, to release the context immediately rather than at GC's convenience, `renderer.forceContextLoss()` followed by dropping the reference to `renderer.domElement`. Modern Three.js also offers `renderer.setAnimationLoop(fn)` and `renderer.setAnimationLoop(null)`, which makes loop cancellation a single call and is the idiomatic replacement for hand-rolled rAF recursion. The correct structural fix is a single long-lived renderer reused across all modal opens, with only the scene contents swapped -- which eliminates the context-exhaustion class of bug entirely. Notably, the same file already gets the analogous Chart.js case right at app.js:779-781 (`if (modalPlddtChartInstance) { modalPlddtChartInstance.destroy(); }`); the Three.js path simply omits the equivalent.

text: [MAJOR] Unpinned Chart.js CDN dependency, a five-year-stale Three.js, and zero Subresource Integrity across all four third-party resources — The page loads four third-party resources over the network and pins none of them safely. index.html:18 is `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js"></script>` -- no version constraint at all. jsDelivr resolves a bare package path to the current latest release: I verified the response header today is `x-jsd-version: 4.5.1` and the served banner reads `Chart.js v4.5.1 ... (c) 2025`. Nothing in the repository records that. When Chart.js 5.x ships, this URL silently begins serving it, and any breaking change to the `new Chart(ctx, {...})` config surface -- Chart.js has made exactly such changes at every major boundary, notably v2→v3 and v3→v4 -- will break both `renderModalPlddtChart` (app.js:797) and `renderBenchmarkChart` (app.js:1057) with no commit, no diff, and no CI signal. index.html:15 pins Three.js to `r128`, published 2021-04-23 per the npm registry; the current release is 0.185.1 (2026-07-01), so the project is 57 minor releases and over five years behind, on a library that has since removed the `examples/js/` UMD directory that index.html:16 depends on. index.html:13 pins Font Awesome 6.4.0, and index.html:11 loads Google Fonts. None of the four carries an `integrity=` attribute -- `grep -c "integrity=" index.html` returns 0 -- and none carries `crossorigin="anonymous"` on the script tags. Nothing is vendored: the repository contains no `vendor/`, `lib/`, or `node_modules/` (the latter is gitignored). Consequence: Two distinct failures. Reproducibility: it is impossible to reconstruct the environment that produced any figure in this repository, today or in five years, because the Chart.js version is not recorded anywhere and the CDN's notion of "latest" moves under the code. A reviewer re-running this page next year may see different rendering, or a blank canvas, and cannot diagnose why. This is precisely the failure mode Rule 6 of the Ten Simple Rules -- "always archive the exact versions of all external programs used" -- exists to prevent. Supply chain: without SRI, the browser executes whatever bytes the CDN returns. A compromise of cdnjs or jsDelivr, or a namespace hijack of the `chart.js` package, injects arbitrary JavaScript into a page that the author is inviting collaborators to open. The unpinned URL widens this further, since a malicious release is picked up automatically with no version bump for anyone to notice. And because the page requires network access at load, it cannot be run at all on an air-gapped or offline machine -- a routine constraint in pharmaceutical and clinical research environments, and a hard blocker for archival reproducibility.

text: Ground truth for SWE-06: The W3C Subresource Integrity specification defines the `integrity` attribute so a browser can verify a fetched resource against a cryptographic digest and refuse to execute it on mismatch; both cdnjs and jsDelivr publish ready-made SRI hashes for every file they serve. For genuine long-term reproducibility, vendoring is stronger than SRI: commit the exact dependency files into the repository so the artifact has no runtime network dependency at all. Rule 6 of "Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research" (DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285) requires archiving exact versions of all external programs. Both Three.js (0.128.0) and Chart.js (4.5.1) are MIT-licensed per their npm registry metadata, as is Font Awesome's code (its icons are CC BY 4.0 and its brand icons carry additional restrictions), so vendoring is permitted provided the license texts travel with the copies.

text: [CRITICAL] No LICENSE file, no AlphaFold3 citation, and DeepMind/Google branding plus a false "Live Connected" status claim that conflict with the AlphaFold Output Terms of Use — Four distinct compliance defects. (1) No license: README.md:4 renders a badge reading `License-Private_Research` linking to the GitHub repo, but no LICENSE, LICENSE.md, or COPYING file exists at the root. A badge is not a license grant; with no license text the work is all-rights-reserved by default, meaning no recipient may legally copy, modify, or redistribute it -- and JOSS requires an OSI-approved license present in the repository as a hard submission criterion. (2) Google/DeepMind branding: README.md:3 renders `[![AlphaFold3](https://img.shields.io/badge/AlphaFold3-DeepMind_Server-00f2fe?style=for-the-badge&logo=google)]`, embedding the Google logo in a badge reading "AlphaFold3 | DeepMind Server"; index.html:30 sets the product subtitle to "DeepMind Structural Pharmacology & AlphaFold3 De Novo Platform", placing "DeepMind" in the masthead of a third-party product; index.html:410 states "Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling". (3) A false connection claim: index.html:42 renders a status pill reading "AlphaFold Server Live Connected" that is an ordinary hyperlink, with no connection of any kind (SWE-01). (4) No citation: `grep -i abramson` across all four files returns nothing -- the AlphaFold3 paper is never cited, in the README, the UI, or the code. Third-party MIT attributions for Three.js, Chart.js, and Font Awesome are likewise entirely absent. Consequence: The branding and the false status claim run directly into terms I retrieved and read in this session. The AlphaFold 3 Output Terms of Use (google-deepmind/alphafold3, OUTPUT_TERMS_OF_USE.md) prohibit use of Output "[t]o misinform, misrepresent or mislead", enumerating "misrepresenting your relationship with Google" and "misrepresenting the origin of" outputs. A page whose masthead reads "DeepMind Structural Pharmacology... Platform", whose README badge carries the Google logo, and whose header asserts "AlphaFold Server Live Connected", is a textbook instance of the conduct that clause names -- and it is aggravated, not mitigated, by the fact that no AlphaFold output is present at all, so nothing is being misrepresented *as* Google's except the platform's own synthetic sine waves. Section 6 of those Terms further requires that anyone distributing Output or disclosing findings from AlphaFold 3 cite Abramson et al.; this project claims AlphaFold3 findings throughout and cites nothing. Separately, the AlphaFold Server Output Terms prohibit use of Output "[i]n connection with any automated system that predicts the binding or interaction of the protein with ligands or peptides, including, but not limited to, Glide or AutoDock" -- language I retrieved verbatim as quoted in google-deepmind/alphafold3 issue #340. A platform that displays per-candidate ΔG and Kd values for peptide-receptor binding alongside AlphaFold Server integration would sit squarely inside that prohibition the moment real Server output entered the pipeline, so this must be resolved before the compute layer is built, not after. Finally, absent a LICENSE the repository cannot be shared, forked, or built upon by anyone, including collaborators the author intends to share it with.

text: [MAJOR] No architectural layering: 36% of the application script is scientific data literals, with unescaped innerHTML injection, two divergent region vocabularies, and no provenance field anywhere — app.js is the application's only script and lines 6-398 -- 393 of 1103 lines, 36% of the file -- are `NATURAL_PRODUCTS_DATA`, `BRAIN_REGIONS_DATA`, `AF3_CANDIDATES`, and `FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA` as inline object literals, interleaved with the DOM handlers that render them. There is no data layer, no compute layer, and no boundary between either and the view. Four concrete consequences are already visible. (i) Divergent vocabularies: `BRAIN_REGIONS_DATA` (app.js:90-121) keys the five regions as `hippocampus, pfc, "basal-forebrain", microglia, astrocytes`, while `FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA` (app.js:138-398) uses `hippocampus, pfc, basal, microglia, astrocyte` -- two of five keys differ, with no shared enum, no constant, and no validation to catch the drift, so the two datasets cannot be joined. (ii) Unescaped injection: 12 `innerHTML` assignments interpolate data straight into markup via template literals (app.js:467, :515, :565, :606, :873, :880 and others), with no escaping or sanitization. The data is static today, so this is not currently exploitable -- but the entire remediation path for this repository involves loading data from external JSON and, plausibly, accepting user-supplied sequences, at which point every one of these 12 sinks becomes a live XSS vector. (iii) Presentation logic is parsing data: app.js:562-563 splits the affinity prose on `|` by position, and app.js:582 does `drug.bindingSites.substring(0, 52)` followed by a literal `...` -- I verified this appends a false ellipsis to 13 of the 25 records whose bindingSites are already shorter than 52 characters (e.g. `"Trem2 Ig domain & Keap1 Kelch domain"`, 36 chars, renders as `"Trem2 Ig domain & Keap1 Kelch domain..."`), and truncates 10 others mid-token (`"...TrkB Ig-like D5 Domain (Asp298, Glu319, Tyr342, Val3..."`). (iv) Control flow reads markup: app.js:535 determines the active filter by string-matching the literal text of a DOM `onclick` attribute (`btn.getAttribute('onclick').includes(...)`), which throws on any button lacking that attribute and couples routing to HTML formatting. Across all four datasets there is not one provenance field: no `method`, no `software_version`, no `date_computed`, no `seed`, no `input_hash`, no `uncertainty`, no `source_doi`. Consequence: The layering violation is why every other finding in this review was possible. Because there is no data layer, there is no schema; because there is no schema, nothing validated the ΔG/Kd pairs (SWE-02) or the non-sequence in drug 24 (SWE-03). Because there is no compute layer, the numbers have no origin, and because there is no provenance field, an expert cannot ask the only question that matters -- "how was -18.4 kcal/mol obtained?" -- and get an answer from the artifact. Practically, the current design means a domain scientist cannot correct a residue assignment without editing JavaScript and risking a syntax error that blanks the entire page; the data cannot be diffed meaningfully in review, cannot be validated in CI, cannot be exported, cannot be consumed by any other tool, and cannot be cited independently of the UI. The vocabulary drift and the false-ellipsis bug are the small, visible symptoms of the same missing boundary.

text: Required fix for SWE-08: Extract app.js:6-398 verbatim into `data/natural_products.json`, `data/brain_regions.json`, `data/candidates.json`, and `data/therapeutics.json`, each governed by a schema under `schemas/`. Add a required `provenance` object to every record -- `{method, software, software_version, container_digest, input_sha256, seed, computed_at, uncertainty}` -- and fail CI on any numeric field lacking one. Replace all 12 `innerHTML` template-literal sinks with `textContent` assignment or explicit DOM construction, or route every interpolation through an escaping helper. Delete the `substring(0, 52) + '...'` truncation at app.js:582 in favour of CSS `text-overflow: ellipsis`, which truncates correctly and never lies. Replace the onclick-attribute string matching at app.js:535 with `data-region` attributes read via `dataset`. Serve the page over HTTP (SWE-04) so `fetch()` of the data files is permitted.

text: Ground truth for SWE-08: The standard layering for a scientific platform is three strictly separated tiers. (1) An immutable, versioned data layer: `data/` holding JSON or Parquet, one record per entity, every value typed with an explicit unit, validated against a committed schema, addressed by content hash, and never edited in place -- corrections land as new versions. (2) A compute layer that reads the data layer and emits derived artifacts, each accompanied by a provenance record naming the tool, its version, the container digest, the input hash, the random seed, and the timestamp; W3C PROV-O (W3C Recommendation, 2013, https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/) is the standard vocabulary and RO-Crate (Data Science, 2022, DOI 10.3233/DS-210053) the standard packaging. (3) A presentation layer that only reads validated artifacts and renders them, containing no data, no domain constants, and no arithmetic. This is the structure behind FAIR principles I3 ("qualified references to other data") and R1.2 ("associated with detailed provenance") in Wilkinson et al. (DOI 10.1038/sdata.2016.18), and behind the modularity guidance in "Best Practices for Scientific Computing" (DOI 10.1371/journal.pbio.1001745).

text: [MINOR] The synthetic confidence visualizations contradict their own legends and contradict each other, with unreachable clamps and a mislabelled PAE axis — Four internal inconsistencies, each verified numerically. (1) Unreachable branches and dead legend: the generator at app.js:791 has an exact analytic range of [89.0, 99.0] over all i and all uppercase letters (I enumerated it: `93 + sin(i*0.4)*4 + (charCode%5)*0.5`, sin term in [-4,4], ASCII term in {0,0.5,1.0,1.5,2.0}). Both clamps that follow -- app.js:792 `if (score > 100) score = 98.6;` and app.js:793 `if (score < 70) score = 76;` -- are therefore unreachable dead code, and the legend bands at index.html:390-391 declaring "Low (50-70)" and "Very Low (<50)" describe states the generator cannot produce. The y-axis is fixed to `min: 50` (app.js:825), so 78% of the plot area is permanently empty. (2) The two "pLDDT" views disagree about the same residue: the 3D sphere colouring at app.js:747-749 keys on amino-acid identity, not on any confidence value -- `if (char === 'G' || char === 'S') resColor = 0x10b981;` (green, legended "High 70-90") and `if (char === 'P' || char === 'D') resColor = 0xf59e0b;` (amber, legended "Low 50-70") -- while the chart assigns those same residues 89.0-98.5, i.e. "Very High". A proline in the modal is simultaneously drawn amber-for-low in the 3D panel and plotted above 90 in the chart directly beside it, under a heading (index.html:377) that calls the 3D colouring a "pLDDT Color Spectrum". (3) Mislabelled PAE axis and unreachable clamp: index.html:397 titles the heatmap "0 - 30 Å", but the maximum value the generator can emit is `(gridSize-1)*0.4 + 3*0.3`, which for the largest grid (45) is 18.5 Å and for a 28-residue sequence is 11.7 Å -- so the clamp at app.js:851 `if (error > 30) error = 30;` is likewise unreachable and the top 38% of the declared range is never used. (4) Silent truncation and aspect distortion: app.js:844 caps the matrix at `Math.min(sequence.length, 45)`, silently dropping residues 46+ for the 47-residue sequence at app.js:143 with no indication in the UI, and renders the square N×N matrix into a 540×220 canvas (index.html:399), giving cells a 2.45:1 aspect ratio so the diagonal of a PAE plot -- the feature practitioners read first -- is not at 45°. Consequence: Taken on their own these are cosmetic; taken together with SWE-01 they show that the synthetic outputs were never checked even for internal coherence, which is corroborating evidence that no one ever compared the rendered figures against what a real AlphaFold output looks like. The concrete misleading effect is specific: a viewer sees a pLDDT chart in which nothing ever drops below 89 and concludes the designs are uniformly high-confidence, when in fact the floor is a property of the constant `93` in the source. And a viewer who trusts the 3D panel's amber colouring will down-weight exactly the prolines and aspartates that the adjacent chart marks as most confident. Two panels in the same modal, under the same heading, give opposite answers about the same residue.

text: Ground truth for SWE-09: Real AlphaFold pLDDT distributions for designed peptides span a wide range and characteristically drop at termini and in flexible linkers -- long poly-glycine-serine linkers of the kind present in these sequences (`GGGGS` repeats at app.js:183, :235, :287, :339, :391) reliably score low, typically 30-60, because they genuinely are disordered. A pLDDT profile that never falls below 89 across a GS-linkered bispecific construct is not a plausible AlphaFold output. The standard AlphaFold colour bands are pLDDT > 90 very high, 70-90 confident, 50-70 low, < 50 very low, and they are applied to the pLDDT value, never to residue identity. Real PAE matrices are plotted on a square canvas with equal axes, scaled to the model's actual maximum (commonly 0-31.75 Å for AlphaFold's binned output), showing the full N×N matrix with no truncation; the block structure off the diagonal is the diagnostic feature and is destroyed by both cropping and aspect distortion.

tags: Research software engineering, reproducibility, and computational drug-discovery infrastructure
text: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3 (2024). The primary AlphaFold3 paper. Defines what an actual AF3 run produces: an mmCIF coordinate file plus a confidence bundle containing per-residue pLDDT, the full N x N PAE matrix, pTM and ipTM. Establishes that pLDDT is the output of a learned confidence head, not an analytic function of sequence. Application here: This is the citation the AlphaFold 3 Output Terms Section 6 require and that the repository never makes. It is also the specification against which app.js:791 and app.js:850 must be replaced: parse pLDDT and PAE from real AF3 confidence JSON, and ship the mmCIF files in a versioned data/structures/ directory rather than generating helices from ASCII codes.

tags: Research software engineering, reproducibility, and computational drug-discovery infrastructure
text: The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship (2016). The canonical statement of Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable data practice. Directly relevant clauses: F1 (globally unique persistent identifiers), I1 (formal shared knowledge representation, i.e. a schema), R1 (rich accurate attributes), R1.1 (clear accessible usage license), R1.2 (detailed provenance). Application here: Supplies the requirements the repository fails on: I1 motivates extracting app.js:6-398 into schema-governed JSON with typed value/unit fields instead of prose strings; R1.1 is the missing LICENSE; R1.2 is the missing provenance object on every ΔG, Kd, and pLDDT; F1 is the missing version tag and DOI.

tags: Research software engineering, reproducibility, and computational drug-discovery infrastructure
text: Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research (2013). Ten operational rules, of which four map exactly onto defects here: Rule 1 (record how every result was produced), Rule 2 (avoid manual data manipulation), Rule 6 (archive the exact versions of all external programs used), Rule 8 (version-control all custom scripts). Application here: Rule 6 is the direct authority for pinning the unpinned Chart.js CDN URL at index.html:18 and recording the exact dependency versions in a committed lockfile. Rule 1 is the authority for attaching a provenance record (tool, version, container digest, input hash, seed, timestamp) to every computed number. Rule 2 condemns the hand-written ΔG/Kd pairs that fail the thermodynamic identity.

tags: Research software engineering, reproducibility, and computational drug-discovery infrastructure
text: Best Practices for Scientific Computing (2014). Consensus engineering practice for research code: plan for mistakes by adding assertions and unit tests, make the data machine-readable, modularize rather than duplicate, automate workflows with a build tool, and use version control on everything. Application here: Justifies the missing tests/ and .github/ directories as substantive defects rather than nice-to-haves. The assertion guidance is the direct remedy for the review's central question -- a typo in a ΔG becomes catchable the moment a CI assertion enforces ΔG = RT ln(Kd) and a JSON Schema enforces pLDDT in [0,100] and sequences matching ^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]+$.

tags: Research software engineering, reproducibility, and computational drug-discovery infrastructure
text: Mol* Viewer: modern web app for 3D visualization and analysis of large biomolecular structures (2021). The production-grade open-source web molecular viewer used by RCSB PDB, PDBe, and the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database. Parses mmCIF/PDB/BinaryCIF natively, renders cartoon/surface/ball-and-stick representations, and supports per-residue colouring by B-factor or pLDDT out of the box. Application here: Replaces the hand-rolled Catmull-Rom tube at app.js:711-732 and app.js:973-994 entirely. Adopting Mol* simultaneously fixes the fabricated geometry (SWE-01), the amino-acid-identity colouring that contradicts the pLDDT chart (SWE-09), and the WebGL context leak (SWE-05), since Mol* manages renderer lifecycle and disposal internally rather than leaving it to ad hoc rAF recursion.

tags: Research software engineering, reproducibility, and computational drug-discovery infrastructure
text: Packaging research artefacts with RO-Crate (2022). A lightweight, widely adopted specification for bundling data, code, and machine-readable provenance metadata into a single citable archive, built on schema.org and JSON-LD. Application here: The concrete packaging format for the provenance requirement in SWE-08. Each AlphaFold3 prediction, each affinity calculation, and each ADMET prediction should be emitted as an RO-Crate carrying the input hash, tool version, container digest, seed, and timestamp, so that every number displayed in the UI traces back to a reproducible computation rather than to an inline literal.

tags: Research software engineering, reproducibility, and computational drug-discovery infrastructure
text: W3C PROV-O: The PROV Ontology (W3C Recommendation) (2013). The W3C standard vocabulary for provenance: Entity, Activity, and Agent, with relations wasGeneratedBy, used, wasDerivedFrom, and wasAttributedTo, expressed in OWL/RDF. Application here: Gives the formal vocabulary for the provenance field that no record in FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA or AF3_CANDIDATES currently has. A ΔG value becomes an Entity that wasGeneratedBy a named calculation Activity which used a specific structure Entity and was attributed to a specific software Agent at a specific version -- making the question 'where did -18.4 kcal/mol come from?' answerable mechanically instead of unanswerable.

text: Best Practices for Alchemical Free Energy Calculations [Article v1.0] (2020). Community best-practice guidance for computing binding free energies: choice of method, force field, sampling protocol, convergence assessment, and mandatory uncertainty estimation, plus what must be reported alongside any ΔG. Application here: Defines the minimum metadata every one of the 25 ΔG values at app.js:146-395 is missing. Once the compute layer exists, each affinity record must carry method, force field, sampling protocol, and a statistical uncertainty; a ΔG with no method and no error bar should fail schema validation. It also frames why the current values cannot be interpreted at all -- there is no way to know whether they were meant as docking scores, MM/GBSA estimates, or aspirational design targets.
